explanation: Outer lanes are longer, which is why runners in the 200 m and 400 m start at staggered positions. Over a full lap, lane eight is more than 50 metres longer than lane one.

claims.text: One lap of the inside lane of a standard outdoor running track measures 400 metres.
A standard outdoor track lap is not 200, 500 or 800 metres.
In the 200 m and 400 m, runners start at staggered positions because outer lanes are longer.
With lanes about 1.22 m wide, a lap of lane eight is more than 50 metres longer than a lap of lane one.

evidence.summaryExcerpt: Length and lanes: World Athletics' technical rules set a standard track at 400 m, with two parallel straights and two bends of equal radius, and say each athlete gets a separate lane for races up to 400 m. The length of a standard running track shall be 400m. It shall consist of two parallel straights and two bends whose radii shall be equal. In all races up to and including 400m, each athlete shall have a separate lane, with a width of 1.22m ± 0.01m, including the lane line on the right. Staggered start: The Facilities Manual says the essential requirement is that every athlete's distance is the same, with no negative tolerance. Lane 8 offsets: A World Athletics marking plan shows lane-by-lane stagger values for lanes 2 through 8, with lane 8 at 26.516 m. However, that row is labelled for the 200 m start, not the 400 m, so it should not be used for a 400 m stagger.

claimResults.note: World Athletics only (Tier A): separate lanes in races up to 400 m, the same distance for every athlete, and stagger values for the 200 m start.
